lanes.summary:
I reviewed the diff against PMAT-4616 (D5) and PMAT-4636 (K1) and found that it fully complies with the tickets' acceptance criteria and directives without weakening any existing gates. 

Key validations:
1. `apr serve` correctly checks if `--context-length` is operator-set in `crates/apr-cli/src/commands/serve/mod.rs`; if unset, it falls back to dynamically sizing the KV by invoking `OwnedQuantizedModelCuda::for_serving`, achieving K1.
2. The dynamic device KV context is computed in `crates/aprender-serve/src/gguf/cuda/session_kv.rs` (via `serving_kv_len`), successfully budgeting the slots within free VRAM and applying the 4096 floor constraint when necessary.
3. Over-context requests in CUDA chat, completions, and stream paths now hit a preflight check (`serve_context_refusal` / `fit_serving_context`) and get an immediate 400 response ("context exceeds ...") rather than returning 500. `ContextLimitExceeded` errors generated later in runtime also securely map to 400 via `generation_error_status`, fulfilling D5.
4. All specified tests (`serve_context_d5.rs` and `serve_kv_limit_k1.rs`, plus the unit tests for `session_kv.rs`) are implemented correctly to enforce these bounds.

The diff accomplishes exactly what both tickets requested.

lanes.summary: The diff implements both tickets faithfully. K1 (PMAT-4636): every CUDA serve path (GGUF, APR, SafeTensors) now routes through the new `serving_cuda_model`/`OwnedQuantizedModelCuda::for_serving`, which sizes the device KV from the model's context within free VRAM via `session_kv::serving_kv_len`, floored at the old fixed 4096 (or the model's context when shorter), and budgets the continuous-batching scheduler's extra slots. `serve::run` now writes `REALIZR_CONTEXT_LENGTH` only when `--context-length` differs from the 4096 default (mirroring an existing PP-14/PP-15 convention already in the same file), letting the auto-sizer take over when unset. D5 (PMAT-4616): a new `serve_context_refusal`/`AppState::serving_context()`/`cap_context()` chain refuses an over-context prompt with 400 before the GPU forward on all three routes the ticket names (chat, completions, stream), and `generation_error_status` (pre-existing) now maps `ContextLimitExceeded` to 400 broadly instead of a hardcoded 500. I traced module paths (`crate::gguf::dense_session` is a `#[path]` re-export, and `handlers_include_01.rs`/`handler_gpu_completion.rs` are both textually `include!`d into the single `handlers` module) to confirm the new cross-file calls actually resolve, and confirmed `max_kv_len()`/`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTH`/`generation_error_status` pre-exist as claimed. New unit and integration tests (`session_kv.rs`, `serve_context_d5.rs`, `serve_kv_limit_k1.rs`, `dense_session.rs` cap_context tests) exercise the stated boundaries (at-limit 200, one-past 400, small-model-gets-whole-context, model-that-fills-card-keeps-floor). I could not execute any test/build (no CUDA hardware, no test runs permitted), so the numeric VRAM-fitting logic and the new CUDA test's runtime pass/fail is asserted from the diff, not measured.

findings.claim: `/v1/batch/completions` (gpu_batch_completions_handler) is not given a pre-flight `serve_context_refusal` check the way chat/completions/stream are, though the ticket's stated three surfaces (chat, completions, stream) are all covered and this handler's underlying `try_cuda_generate` calls `generate_gpu_resident` directly, preserving the typed `ContextLimitExceeded` error so `generation_error_status` alone maps it to 400 without needing a pre-flight (unlike the scheduler-channel paths, whose errors are stringified). Not a contradiction of the AC as written, just a narrower surface than 'every CUDA serve path' might suggest.
findings.failure_scenario: A batch of prompts submitted to /v1/batch/completions with one prompt over the serving context relies on the typed-error path working correctly through `generate_gpu_resident`/dense_session rather than being independently pre-flight-checked; if that typed-error path ever regresses to a raw GPU fault (as the D5 bug originally was for the scheduler-channel paths), this route would silently start 500ing again with no test catching it.
